apparatus.title: OPUS SECTILE
apparatus.lead: Cosmatesque, laid before the high altar in 1268
apparatus.reading: The governing figure is the quincunx: four roundels about a fifth, bound by one band that loops each and crosses itself between them. Here the quincunx stands in a square turned on its point, four great roundels fill the corners it leaves, and a broad border runs twenty more around the whole. No two panels are cut alike — the four orbiting roundels are a circle, a hexagon, a heptagon and an octagon.
apparatus.quote: In the year of Christ a thousand, twice a hundred, and twelve, with sixty, four years taken away: the third King Henry, the City, Odoricus and the abbot set these porphyry stones together.
apparatus.attribution: The border, read sunwise from the top, set in brass letters in the Purbeck
apparatus.settingOutNote: Struck with cord and compass before a stone was cut: the square and its border, the square turned in it, and the circles every roundel and every loop of the band is cut to.
